products.name: go-schedule
products.context: Prepared v2.0.2 source, independent local/remote daemons; Apache 2.0. Public packages remain v2.0.1.

products.name: JAMS
products.context: Current Core/Advanced offering and vendor documentation; installed Windows-server scheduler with platform agents; entitlements vary.

products.name: ActiveBatch
products.context: Current vendor client-server platform; licensed cross-platform agents; Non-Cluster Failover is an add-in and interface entitlements vary by version.

products.name: ScriptRunner
products.context: ScriptRunner Enterprise 8 and current Microsoft/PowerShell platform material; licensed workflows/connectors and customer deployment context apply.

products.name: Control-M
products.context: Control-M 9.0.22 self-hosted documentation and Automation API; SaaS and API-version prerequisites differ.

products.name: Azure Logic Apps
products.context: Consumption and Standard; Standard cloud/ASE/hybrid options and preview capabilities differ.

products.name: Resolve Actions
products.context: Current platform brief; Actions cloud/hybrid Remote Executor documentation and Actions Pro 8.1 documentation, with separate edition, deployment and licensing prerequisites.

products.name: OpCon
products.context: OpCon 26.0 On-Prem core plus current vendor-owned CLI; VisualCron/RPA and MFT integration documentation is separately scoped, with license and deployment prerequisites.

goschedule.note: Readable recurrence, supported five/six-field cron and explicit timezone/DST policies.

jams.note: Natural-language dates, fixed intervals and recurring execution windows; timezone and calendar settings are configurable.

activebatch.note: Calendar, timezone and business-day date/time scheduling, with trigger- and constraint-based options.

scriptrunner.note: Central one-off and recurring scheduling for Actions; available patterns and execution targets depend on configuration.

controlm.note: Control-M 9.0.22 supports calendar/day criteria, time windows and cyclic execution at intervals or specified times.

logicapps.note: Consumption and Standard support recurrence scheduling; advanced options and missed-run behavior depend on trigger type and hosting limits.

resolve.note: Actions workflows can run on schedules; recurrence dialect and deployment settings are product-specific.

opcon.note: OpCon 26.0 on-premises frequencies define recurring calendar rules, offsets and exclusions used to build job and schedule instances.

goschedule.note: External trigger keys, file/directory watchers and task-completion sources.

jams.note: Job-completion, file, variable and email triggers can submit jobs when their configured conditions occur.

activebatch.note: File, email, predecessor completion, startup, queue and web-service events can initiate workflows; integrations affect individual sources.

scriptrunner.note: Enterprise 8 workflows include webhook triggers; web-service connectors allow external systems to initiate Actions/workflows, subject to integration licensing.

controlm.note: Control-M 9.0.22 events release successor jobs after predecessor completion and other prerequisites; global events span Control-M/Servers.

logicapps.note: Consumption and Standard workflows start from request, webhook or connector events; connector and hosting availability vary.

resolve.note: Actions workflows can start from events, alerts or incidents; integrations determine the available signals.

opcon.note: OpCon 26.0 core supports status, agent-feedback and expression-triggered events; file/MFT and VisualCron initiation retain their integration prerequisites.

goschedule.note: Durable success/failure/any completion chains; no claim of a full visual branching workflow language.

jams.note: Sequences support ordered and parallel tasks; Workflow Designer activities provide conditional execution paths.

activebatch.note: Reusable Job Steps compose cross-system workflows, including dependency-based orchestration.

scriptrunner.note: Enterprise 8 provides visual sequential/parallel workflows, conditions and retained execution state around reusable Actions in Microsoft/PowerShell environments.

controlm.note: Control-M 9.0.22 defines predecessor/successor job and folder dependencies, including global events between servers.

logicapps.note: Consumption and Standard compose triggers and actions with conditional follow-up actions and scopes based on success, failure or other statuses.

resolve.note: Actions includes workflow conditions; the platform brief also describes parallel execution.

opcon.note: OpCon 26.0 core supports job dependencies within/across schedules and dates, including success/failure completion conditions.

goschedule.note: Wails desktop, authoring/operational CLI with structured acknowledgements and corrective diagnostics, plus JSON API. CLI QA and opt-in pre-entry incident capture are source-tree maintainer tools.

jams.note: Web and thick clients with .NET and REST APIs; installation and entitlement context apply.

activebatch.note: Console, web/self-service interfaces, SOAP/REST Web Services, PowerShell/COM and Linux/UNIX CLI; version and download requirements vary.

scriptrunner.note: Portal operations and REST/Web Service integration with configurable Swagger exposure; workflow UI depends on the licensed feature.

controlm.note: Control-M 9.0.22 provides Client/Web operator interfaces and Automation API CLI/REST access for Jobs-as-Code and management.

logicapps.note: Visual designer and JSON definitions are available; Standard adds local Visual Studio Code run/debug/deploy tooling, while deployment commands depend on the resource model.

resolve.note: Visual/API authoring plus script, SSH and CLI activities; CLI activity does not establish a standalone operator CLI.

opcon.note: OpCon offers browser operations and a Windows/Linux REST-backed CLI; the CLI requires OpCon 21.x+, Java 11 and a REST API license.

goschedule.note: Enrolled independent daemons, All Systems, search and portable configuration. S139 actual host/WSL connection tests were blocked by the test environment.

jams.note: Central scheduler with local/remote platform agents and agent-pool queues; supported platform/type combinations vary.

activebatch.note: Distributed scheduler with cross-platform execution agents for physical, virtual and cloud hosts; agent licensing and platform support apply.

scriptrunner.note: Managed remote targets and reusable target collections support fleet execution across configured Microsoft/PowerShell systems.

controlm.note: Control-M 9.0.22 centrally schedules and tracks work on agents or agentless hosts; self-hosted, SaaS and Unified View contexts differ.

logicapps.note: Connectors integrate cloud and on-premises systems; Standard hybrid can run local workflows on Azure Arc-enabled infrastructure with Azure-connected management.

resolve.note: Actions connects its cloud tenant to on-premises systems through installed Remote Executors; Windows-server and connectivity prerequisites apply.

opcon.note: OpCon 26.0 centrally submits work through target-platform agents; machine groups allow available-agent selection and load balancing.

goschedule.note: Execution history/logs, durable webhook and SMTP delivery with recipient-aware retries, plus optional running-desktop popups.

jams.note: Active Monitor, completed execution history and logs, with email notifications and recovery-job responses.

activebatch.note: Workflow status monitoring, customizable alerts, execution views, reporting and configurable SLA thresholds.

scriptrunner.note: Execution reports/logs, live monitoring, server event records and notification connectors; Enterprise 8 adds nested workflow reports.

controlm.note: Control-M 9.0.22 monitoring exposes job state, activity logs and output; alert operations are separately configurable.

logicapps.note: Consumption and Standard expose trigger/run history and alerts; richer Azure Monitor diagnostics require configuration, and Standard stateless history differs.

resolve.note: Platform audit records are documented; Actions Pro 8.1 stores runbook results and provides component monitoring and failure alerts.

opcon.note: OpCon 26.0 provides schedule/job history, server logs and notifications triggered by machine, schedule or job status changes.

goschedule.note: Actor capabilities, delegated credentials and management audit records.

jams.note: Object permissions and execution credentials, plus audit trails and job-history logging; expanded security/audit offerings are edition-dependent.

activebatch.note: Directory-backed object permissions and virtual roots, with object audit trails, revision history and changesets.

scriptrunner.note: Role-based delegation, managed credential/vault integrations, configuration change tracking and action audit/report records.

controlm.note: Control-M 9.0.22 roles scope interface/object operations; audit and annotation coverage and retention are configurable across authentication, jobs, definitions, accounts and configuration.

logicapps.note: Azure RBAC scopes Consumption/Standard access. Control-plane Activity Log is collected by default; workflow runtime diagnostics and extended audit retention require configuration.

resolve.note: The platform brief documents role-scoped permissions and audit records for automation and user activity.

opcon.note: OpCon 26.0 roles scope functions and objects; audit records track user/database updates across accounts, roles, machines, jobs and schedules.

goschedule.note: Optional local and authenticated remote MCP with explicit authority.

jams.note: JAMS Web MCP queries jobs/failures, submits jobs and manages existing runs as the signed-in user; AI job/workflow authoring remains roadmap work.

activebatch.note: Native ActiveBatch MCP availability remains unestablished. The retained 2026-11-06 assessment must not be inferred from Redwood RunMyJobs MCP announcements.

scriptrunner.note: Release availability remains unresolved: the April 2026 Enterprise 8 launch calls MCP planned while the February trigger article describes a server as present; retained assessment date is 2026-11-06.

controlm.note: Retained 2026-11-06 preview assessment; later retrievals conflict on production status and API prerequisites. Current general availability is not established.

logicapps.note: Preview API Center integration exposes Standard connector actions as MCP tools: one connector per server and one action per tool; built-in service-provider and custom connectors are excluded.

resolve.note: Actions Pro 8.1 Dynamic MCP exposes selected published runbooks through configured endpoints with selectable authentication and deployment state.

opcon.note: MCP availability remains unestablished in the retained 2026-11-06 assessment; current cloud-only Otto REST tooling does not establish an on-premises MCP endpoint.

goschedule.note: Independent-daemon management does not provide clustered execution ownership/failover.

jams.note: A configured secondary scheduler takes over after missed heartbeats; jobs executing on the failed scheduler host can still fail.

activebatch.note: The Non-Cluster Failover Add-In provides active-standby scheduler heartbeat monitoring with automatic or manual takeover.

scriptrunner.note: Redundant execution Server Groups and target-collection failover are documented; scheduler ownership and recovery of in-flight work are not established here.

controlm.note: Control-M 9.0.22 self-hosted secondary-host failover is documented; automatic/default versus manual takeover depends on database topology.

logicapps.note: Consumption has zone redundancy in supported regions; Standard requires suitable zone/storage configuration. Cross-region recovery needs routing/activation design, and in-flight state stays regional.

resolve.note: Actions Pro 8.1 documents clustered orchestration and state replication. Actions hybrid executors route subsequent work around unavailable devices; neither source establishes in-flight workload recovery.

opcon.note: OpCon 26.0 supports configured primary/secondary service failover, automatically or manually; database topology matters and returning to primary requires manual intervention.

goschedule.note: Apache 2.0 source; locally operated daemons without a hosted account requirement.

jams.note: Commercial licensed Windows-server software, deployable locally or on AWS/Azure; the vendor explicitly distinguishes it from SaaS.

activebatch.note: Commercial subscription software with distributed client/server deployment; exact configuration, add-ins and license terms are vendor-quoted.

scriptrunner.note: Commercial term/subscription object-code software installed in customer IT infrastructure; source-code access is excluded and feature/connector scope is licensed.

controlm.note: Source/licensing terms for selected self-hosted 9.0.22 remain unestablished; the 2026-10-27 assessment is retained because current retrieval did not verify them.

logicapps.note: Azure service with metered Consumption and plan-based Standard models; Standard hybrid uses customer infrastructure and remains Azure-managed and billed.

resolve.note: The platform brief lists SaaS, on-premises, hybrid and container models; Actions hybrid requires cloud connectivity, and edition/license terms remain unestablished.

opcon.note: OpCon 26.0 on-premises requires a license file with machine- or task-based limits; CLI REST licensing and integration entitlements are separate. Source rights remain unestablished.

opportunities.note: Clustered execution is explicitly owner-deferred under #20 and #186. Independent-daemon management does not supply execution ownership or failover, and this comparison does not authorize implementation.
